92.0.0.en: 1- It is a good thing to give thanks unto the Lord, and to sing praises unto thy name, O most High:

92.0.1.en: 1- At its beginning the Psalm declares the importance of thanking God, praising Him and confessing His greatness, and this in turn moves the heart and the tongue to sing to His holy name, because He is God, high above all creatures, for He is their Creator, and therefore man, the leader of creation, should praise Him and glorify Him at all times.

92.0.2.en: 2- The Church takes care to begin all her liturgical prayers with praise of God, so she prays the prayer of thanksgiving. It is noticed that this verse and the one after it are prayed by the Church every day in the piece found in the prayer of Sleep, which begins “Vouchsafe, O Lord,” for these two verses are at the end of this piece. St. Athanasius the Apostolic composed and arranged this piece.

92.1.0.en: 2- To shew forth thy lovingkindness in the morning, and thy faithfulness every night,

92.1.1.en: Morning: early, that is, the dawn of the new day.

92.1.2.en: 1- Whoever thanks God and sings to His holy name, God grants him His mercy all his life, that is, in the morning and throughout the day. And as long as we are alive, that is, in the day, we have an opportunity to praise God, because in death there is none who remembers God and thanks Him. Also in the day, that is, throughout life, man can repent of his sins, and so obtain God's mercy and make it known, that is, thank God and call people to faith and repentance to enjoy God's mercy. So the day is the opportunity to enjoy God's mercy, care and love, and man's thanks to God increase. And the day is the times free from trials, in which there is an opportunity for spiritual growth and a relationship at rest with God.

92.2.0.en: 3- Upon an instrument of ten strings, and upon the psaltery, upon the playing of the lute.

92.2.1.en: 1- The writer of the Psalm is not content, in calling people to thank God and sing to Him with their mouths, but calls them to be accompanied in the hymns by musical instruments, and mentions here three kinds of stringed instruments that accompany praise. And this means variety in the instruments, which signifies the variety of kinds of thanksgiving, because God's works are very many, and their kinds are countless.

92.2.2.en: 2- The ten strings signify the Ten Commandments, and also the five outward senses, that is, the bodily ones, and the five inward senses, that is, the psychological ones. And this means that man praises with the spirit and with the body, and whoever keeps the commandments of God and lives by them can thank God, and his heart longs to praise Him.

92.3.0.en: 4- For thou, Lord, hast made me glad through thy work: I will triumph in the works of thy hands.

92.3.1.en: Whoever loves God, and his tongue is loosed in praise and thanksgiving, his heart is enlightened, and God's love for him is revealed through His works, so his heart rejoices and exults. And the more his thanksgiving increases, his enlightenment and his seeing of the works of God increase, so he thanks more and rejoices.

92.4.0.en: 5- O Lord, how great are thy works! and thy thoughts are very deep.

92.4.1.en: 1- At the end of this passage, the writer of the Psalm, before the multitude of God's works and their variety and His care for His children, declares that His works are very great, so that he expressed it by his saying, “how great are thy works,” that is, he is unable to know and appreciate this greatness. For they are greater than any works that men do. And consequently they deserve constant thanksgiving.

92.4.2.en: 2- And when the writer of the Psalm contemplated the thoughts of God that are behind His works he found them very deep, and indeed he was not able to express how deep they are, so he said “very deep,” as St. Paul the Apostle said, “how unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past finding out!” (Rom 11:33), and since the thoughts of God are very deep, man must submit to God and obey His commandments and praise His greatness.

92.4.3.en: Take care to thank God at the end of every day for His providence so that your heart may be enlightened and you see God, and enjoy seeing His works, and your heart is filled with joy.

92.5.s.en: (2) The weakness of the wicked before the strength of the righteous

92.5.0.en: 6- A brutish man knoweth not; neither doth a fool understand this.

92.5.1.en: 1- The fool and the brutish are the two who neither know nor keep the commandments of God, and consequently they have no spiritual enlightenment, so they do not see the greatness of God's works, and do not glorify Him or thank Him. And on the contrary, in pride they claim knowledge and understanding, and walk in evil, and make light of God.

92.5.2.en: 2- The fool and the brutish, having lost the inward senses, that is, understanding and wisdom, walk in an animal, instinctive manner, and interpret God's judgments wrongly, and become vexed with God and murmur against Him. They do not submit to the will of God nor trust in Him, so their conduct is foolish and leads them to destruction.

92.6.0.en: 7- When the wicked spring as the grass, and when all the workers of iniquity do flourish; it is that they shall be destroyed for ever:

92.6.1.en: 1- Here the writer of the Psalm decrees that the end of the wicked is eternal destruction, and consequently we should not be preoccupied with their success in this life, for it will pass, and we should not be troubled by their pride and boasting in this success, for it is temporary, and even if it lasts it is not for more than this life, but the other life is eternal torment for them.

92.6.2.en: 2- Since life is temporary, and our life resembles the grass and its flowers, which even if they appear beautiful quickly wither, all this leads us to repentance and to preparing for eternal life, so we live with God on earth, that we may have a place in heaven, and be rid of all our evils.

92.7.0.en: 8- But thou, Lord, art most high for evermore.

92.7.1.en: 1- The wicked cling to earthly desires and so descend downward, but the righteous cling to God the Most High, and to all the spiritual things that lift them to Him, so they rise every day to heavenly things.

92.7.2.en: 2- God is most high for ever, and everyone who lives with God enjoys eternity with Him, but the wicked exalt themselves in this life, and their greatness ends with death, so they enter the lowest parts of the earth, that is, Hades.

92.8.0.en: 9- For, lo, thine enemies, O Lord, for, lo, thine enemies shall perish; all the workers of iniquity shall be scattered.

92.8.1.en: 1- Here the writer of the Psalm affirms that whoever commits sin is an enemy of God; if he repents God accepts him, but if he persists in sin he is a true enemy of God, and a follower of Satan who is hostile to God, and is a worker of iniquity, that is, persists in iniquity and clings to it in his heart.

92.8.2.en: 2- These wicked who cling to sin perish, because they clung to the perishing world and so perish with it, that is, go to eternal destruction. And they are scattered like chaff before the wind, that is, they have no value however they appear in greatness and authority in this world, because they are empty as regards God, and their hearts are full of evil.

92.9.0.en: 10- But my horn shalt thou exalt like the horn of a wild ox: I am anointed with fresh oil. 11- Mine eye also shall see them that watch for me, and mine ears shall hear of them that rise up against me with evil.

92.9.1.en: On the other side God gives the righteous many blessings, which are:

92.9.2.en: 1- They receive strength, symbolized by the upraised horn, and no sacrifice was offered to God except one with an upraised horn, because it signifies Christ the strong, crucified to redeem us.

92.9.3.en: 2- They receive vitality, symbolized by the fresh oil, so they move with energy and do their spiritual and material works with zeal, and prosper in all they do (Ps 1).

92.9.4.en: 3- They receive discernment, so they know the plots of the enemy and Satan and all that follows him, and they are on guard against him by taking refuge in God through all the spiritual practices. Those who watch them are the wicked who want to snare them and make them fall into errors, so God gives them sight, hearing and knowledge of everything that is plotted against them, and delivers them from the hands of the wicked, and they live in tranquility.

92.9.5.en: Trust in the power of God that supports you and works in you so that you are not troubled by the plots of the wicked around you, and on the contrary have compassion on them and pray for them, that God may give them repentance so that they know God and live with Him.

92.10.s.en: (3) The blessings of God to the righteous

92.10.0.en: 12- The righteous shall flourish like the palm tree: he shall grow like a cedar in Lebanon.

92.10.1.en: 1- The writer of the Psalm likens the righteous man to the palm tree that rises toward heaven, and it signifies elevation above earthly things and preoccupation with heavenly things, and likewise the cedar tree that grows in Lebanon, for it rises toward heaven.

92.10.2.en: 2- The palm tree needs a long time to grow, a reference to the spiritual striving by which man reaches God. As for the grass that also flourishes (v. 7), it is quick to grow and quick to pass away.

92.10.3.en: 3- The palm tree's roots extend to great depths to feed the tall trunk, a symbol of the importance of spiritual depth, and it gives sweet fruit, the dates, in their different colors, which signify the spiritual fruits, and its branches rise toward heaven like one who lifts his hands in prayer.

92.10.4.en: 4- The cedar is a tree whose wood is strong and which lives hundreds of years, a reference to the strength of the life of believers, and their remaining for ever in the Kingdom. And the cedar grows in Lebanon, which is of the Gentiles, a prophecy of the Gentiles' faith in Christ.

92.11.0.en: 13- Those that be planted in the house of the Lord shall flourish in the courts of our God.

92.11.1.en: The planter who plants these trees is the Lord, so He plants His children in His house, that they may grow and flourish. And everyone who is rooted in the house of the Lord, that is, in holy worship, brings forth flowers and spiritual fruits on earth and they are completed in heaven. And as long as they are planted in the house of the Lord, God satisfies them and makes them grow and cares for them, so Satan cannot draw them away from God.

92.12.0.en: 14- They shall still bring forth fruit in old age; they shall be fat and flourishing;

92.12.1.en: 1- The righteous are full of vitality and spiritual satisfaction, “fat and flourishing,” and consequently they have spiritual fruits. These fruits do not leave them, not only in the days of their youth, but even in their old age, so they glorify God and draw the souls of others to Him, and satisfy them from the overflow of the satisfaction with which they are filled. For the righteous are a light to the world by their righteous life.

92.12.2.en: 2- The body weakens when man reaches old age, but the spirit is renewed as the eagle's youth is renewed (Ps 103:5), for the righteous are in a constant spiritual youth, like the palm tree that gives its sweet fruit in its old age; and likewise the cedar becomes strong wood when the tree grows old.

92.13.0.en: 15- To shew that the Lord is upright: he is my rock, and there is no unrighteousness in him. When the righteous bear fruit throughout their lives they glorify God, and declare by their works that God is upright and just and wrongs no one. For He rewards the righteous with good fruits, but as for the wicked, their flourishing and greatness are short-lived like the grass (v. 7); for the true, complete fruit is in eternity, so the righteous are blessed in the Kingdom, but the wicked are tormented in eternal destruction.

92.13.1.en: Be patient in your striving, confident of the grace of God that supports you and pours spiritual fruits over you, so that you live in happiness on earth, and in unspeakable glory in heaven.

92.13.2.en: God the Almighty, the Holy, the Glorified. “The Lord reigneth, he is clothed with majesty ...” (v. 1)

92.13.4.en: 1- Its writer: there are two opinions:

92.13.5.en: a - The Holy Bible does not mention a title for it, so it is considered one of the orphan Psalms, that is, those whose writer is not mentioned.

92.13.6.en: b- In the Septuagint translation there is a title for this Psalm, which is “A blessing, a song of praise of David, for the day before the Sabbath, when the earth was inhabited.” From this we learn the following:

92.13.7.en: That its writer is David the prophet, as evidenced by the similarity of the verses of this Psalm to the song that David repeated when he moved the ark of the covenant of God to Jerusalem (1 Chr 16:30-33).

92.13.8.en: It announces the redemption of Christ that was accomplished on Friday, before the Sabbath, so the earth was inhabited by believers in the New Testament from the Jews and the Gentiles, that is, from all the earth, and the Jews refused to put this title, because it points clearly to Christ the Redeemer on the Cross.

92.13.9.en: 2- When was it written? When David moved the ark of the covenant of God from the house of Obed-edom to Jerusalem, and they were praising with this Psalm while it was being moved.

92.13.10.en: 3- This Psalm is considered one of the royal Psalms, that is, those that speak about the Lord the King, and some consider it an introduction to these Psalms, which begin from Psalm 95-100 and they call them the “theocratic” Psalms, that is, those that speak about God the King.

92.13.11.en: 4- This Psalm is also one of the Messianic Psalms, for it speaks about Christ risen from the dead by the power of His divinity, His majesty and His might, and it does not mention anything about the sufferings of Christ.

92.13.12.en: 5- This Psalm is also one of the liturgical Psalms, that is, those which the people used to repeat under the leadership of the Levites on the eve of the Sabbath and at the feast of harvest.

92.13.13.en: 6- The priest in the New Testament repeats this Psalm when he puts on his priestly vestments to begin the service of the Liturgy, so that he remembers that he represents Christ the King in the Liturgy with all His glory and greatness, and so is reverent before Him, and comes forward with the fear of God to the service of the Holy Mysteries.

92.13.14.en: 7- This Psalm is found at the end of the prayer of the Sixth Hour, in which we remember the crucified Christ, who reigned on the wood of the Cross to redeem us, so we glorify Him, for He condescended from His greatness to lift our sins from us.

93.0.0.en: 1- The Lord reigneth, he is clothed with majesty; the Lord is clothed with strength, wherewith he hath girded himself: the world also is stablished, that it cannot be moved.

93.0.1.en: Girded himself: wrapped it around his waist like a belt.

93.0.2.en: 1- Christ hid His divinity by His Incarnation and did not appear as a king of great majesty except in His miracles, and His teaching with authority, but His power and greatness appeared clearly in His Resurrection from the dead, and His appearing in a luminous body to His disciples, then He ascended to the heavens in great glory.

93.0.3.en: 2- The Lord reigned on the Cross when He bound Satan, and brought those who believe in Him out of Hades, and brought them up to Paradise, and reigned over the hearts of those who believe in Him, and thus He girded Himself with strength in delivering His children from the bondage of Satan in Hades, and lifted them to Paradise, to reign over them for ever. And in the Kingdom His complete and eternal reign appears.

93.0.4.en: 3- The earth, “the world,” God established in its rotation on itself and around the sun, and it also signifies the steadfastness of believers in Christ despite the changes of life around them and the wars of the devil, for God establishes them in faith in Him, and as for the new earth and the new heaven, that is, the new world and the Kingdom of Heaven, God establishes them for ever.

93.0.5.en: 4- When God girds Himself with strength He declares that He is the leader of the war against Satan, and this reassures His children who believe in Him that He protects them, so they are filled with hope however much they fall or are weak, and they are strengthened to resist the devil and triumph over him by the power of God.

93.1.0.en: 2- Thy throne is established of old: thou art from everlasting.

93.1.1.en: 1- In this verse the writer of the Psalm declares the eternity of God, for although He became incarnate in the fullness of time to redeem mankind, He has existed from eternity before all creatures, because He is their Creator.

93.1.2.en: 2- The throne of God signifies His Incarnation, for it was in God's mind to become incarnate from the beginning and from eternity, and He accomplished it in the fullness of time when He was born of the Virgin.

93.1.3.en: 3- The throne of God is also a symbol of those who believe in Him, in whom He dwells and over whose hearts He reigns.

93.1.4.en: 4- On Good Friday, in the Church of the New Testament, at the burial of Christ in the twelfth hour, we remember the greatness of God and His throne that has existed from eternity, so we say the Psalm “Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever,” with its well-known long melody.

93.1.5.en: God wants to reign over your heart to give you tranquility, and to gladden your heart by His dwelling in it, so make room for Him by many prayers and by reading His holy word in the Bible every day.

93.2.0.en: 3- The floods have lifted up, O Lord, the floods have lifted up their voice; the floods lift up their waves.

93.2.1.en: Their roaring: the sound of the crashing of their waves, and it is a loud sound.

93.2.2.en: 1- Nature glorifies God, so the floods (rivers) come forward as representatives of it and their waves crash, to praise God their Creator.

93.2.3.en: 2- The voice of the rivers signifies the Apostles who preached the name of Christ in the whole world, and also signifies the men of God and the prophets in the Old Testament who proclaimed the divine truth, and also the priests and servants through the generations until now who proclaim the name of God, in addition to the martyrs who proclaimed with a loud voice their love for God by shedding their blood for Him, and likewise the ascetics who inhabited the deserts and sent up voices of praise and glorification to God. This is the effect of the Holy Spirit who flows like living rivers in the hearts of those who believe in Him.

93.3.0.en: 4- The Lord on high is mightier than the noise of many waters, yea, than the mighty waves of the sea.

93.3.1.en: Mighty: many waters that flood what is around them, that is, cover it.

93.3.2.en: 1- Nature also represents the seas, which glorify God by their voices and the abundance of their waters, and are able to flood the dry land; all this is a declaration of their power, but God their Creator is mightier than they and more able without limit. So the power of the seas is merely a small expression of the power of God the Creator.

93.3.3.en: 2- The seas signify the lives of believers and servants through the generations, which flood the dry land, that is, paganism, so the waters cover the hearts far from God, and draw them to Him, to declare that God is mightier and more able than the hardness of the hearts of men, and by His love He draws these hearts to Himself.

93.3.4.en: Trust in the power of God that is in you to live by His commandments, and offer your love to all around you however much they wrong you, for love is strong as death, and cannot be resisted if it comes from your heart, so continue in it in every way.

93.4.0.en: 5- Thy testimonies are very sure: holiness becometh thine house, O Lord, for ever.

93.4.1.en: 1- The testimonies of God are all the prophecies and types that were mentioned in the Old Testament about Christ. And all of them have been fulfilled, for of God's word not one letter can pass away, and consequently we should hold fast to the promises of God, because they are sure.

93.4.2.en: 2- If God is true in every word He says to us, then we should enter His holy house, which remains holy not only on earth, represented in the temple of Solomon, and after it the Church in the New Testament, but also in the Kingdom of Heaven. And if holiness becomes the house of God, then we must purify our hearts by repentance and by love for everyone when we enter the Church, and for this reason the priest repeats this Psalm when he puts on the priestly vestments to begin the prayers of the Divine Liturgy, to remember the holiness of the house of God in which he will stand and raise his voice in prayer before Him.

93.4.3.en: Take care to pray and repeat the Psalms while you are on your way to the Church, so you say the Psalm “I was glad when they said unto me” (Ps 122). And when you reach the Church you pray at the door and repeat the Psalm “How amiable are thy tabernacles ...” (Ps 84) and you prostrate before the sanctuary and say “But as for me, in the multitude of thy mercy ...” (Ps 5). And you stand in reverence before God the Holy asking His forgiveness for all your sins, and you attend to the prayer to share with the heavenly ones in praising His holy name.

93.4.4.en: God, the Deliverer of the righteous and the Avenger of the wicked. “O Lord God, to whom vengeance belongeth; O God, to whom vengeance belongeth, shew thyself” (v. 1). Introduction:

93.4.5.en: 1- Its writer: there are two opinions:

93.4.6.en: a - This Psalm has no title in the Beirut version, so it is considered one of the orphan Psalms, that is, those without a title.

93.4.7.en: b - In the Septuagint translation there is a title for this Psalm and it mentions that it is David's.

93.4.8.en: 2- In the title of the Septuagint translation it is mentioned that this Psalm is for “the fourth day,” so it used to be recited on the fourth day in the tabernacle of meeting, or the temple of Solomon. And perhaps this Psalm is a prophecy about God's vengeance on Judas Iscariot, who betrayed Christ and conspired with the Jews to deliver Him on the fourth day.

93.4.9.en: 3- The subject of this Psalm is the distress of the people of God from those who oppress them, and they ask God to rescue them, for they are peaceable and do not take revenge on those who oppress them, but ask for God's intervention.

93.4.10.en: 4- It appears from this Psalm that God does not keep trials from His children, but He listens attentively to their prayers, comforts them, and punishes those who oppress them.

93.4.11.en: 5- This Psalm is not found in the prayer of the Agpeya.
